predecessors.name: Spanish Empire
predecessors.text: Spanish South America without Cuyo and the Santo Domingo states of Venezuela

ledger.x: 1542 (20 November): the New Laws create the Viceroyalty of Peru.
1717 (27 May): the first Viceroyalty of New Granada is created from Peru's northern territories.
1723 (5 November): New Granada is suppressed and Peru takes its land back.
1739 (20 August): New Granada is restored, with Quito and Panama.
1776 (1 August): Charcas and Buenos Aires pass to the new Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata.
ledger.cpn: Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata
Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata

ledger.x: 1810: Upper Peru is annexed to Peru.
ledger.cpn: Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata

ledger.x: 1814 (3 August): a junta under Pumacahua takes Cuzco.
1820 (7 September): San Martin's Liberation Expedition lands at Pisco.
1821: the viceroy moves the capital from Lima to Cusco.
1821 (June): the Pisco landing zone becomes patriot land with the entry into Lima (the contest that began with the landing of September 1820).
1824: the last campaign in the highlands, Junin and Ayacucho.
1824 (9 December): Ayacucho ends the royalist war.
1824 (30 December): the Viceroyalty of Peru is dissolved.

wars.name: Cuzco rebellion of 1814
wars.outcome: A criollo and indigenous junta under Mateo Pumacahua held Cuzco from 3 August 1814; royal forces crushed it by mid-1815.

wars.name: Peruvian War of Independence
wars.outcome: The Liberation Expedition landed at Pisco on 7 September 1820, entered Lima on 27 June 1821 and proclaimed independence on 28 July 1821; Bolivar's campaign won at Junin and Ayacucho (9 December 1824); the royalist holdouts, the Real Felipe fortress at Callao…
